text.p: In world commodity markets on Friday night, the gold price slumped through support at US$335 an ounce to end at new four and a quarter year lows on talk of new Australian hedging and fund selling.
Metal prices were mostly steady in London.
Oil prices eased back on doubts about the OPEC oil supply deal designed to lift prices.
Wheat prices fell sharply on new U.S. harvests.
The CRB index fell 0.07 points to 239.33.

Overall base metal activity on the London Metal Exchange (LME) was fairly nondescript on Friday, although zinc reached a new 6-3/4 year high, while nickel slumped to a 6-1/2 month low. Traders said zinc continued to build on the speculative buying seen so far in the current bull-run, helped by clearing $1,420 - the previous high - and then $1,426. Prices peaked at $1,430 a tonne before settling at $1,428, up $16 from Thursday's kerb close. Nickel belatedly reacted to overnight news of a tentative deal at Inco's strike-bound Sudbury mine, and fell below $7,000, triggering some sell-stops down to a low of $6,930.

Some support is expected around $6,900, so prices edged off the lows to end at $6,970, still $100 lower. Copper business was transacted within a comparatively tight $28 range, with the market absorbing a mini sell-off down to a $2,400 low. The spreads remains tight ahead of next Wednesday's July options declarations, so the market will remain nervous in the short-term. Last trade was at $2,418, up $20. Aluminium tended to mirror copper's movements, and edged up from mid-afternoon lows, finishing at $1,575, down just $2.
Oil prices closed higher on Friday as traders shrugged off doubts about whether major OPEC oil producers will be able to restrain oil sales and focused on more immediate delays in shipments by Iraq.

At the New York Mercantile Exchange, crude oil for August delivery closed 37 cents a barrel higher at $19.46. Iraq was to start its second six-month period on June 8, but oil sales have been held up until technicalities surrounding the distribution of aid are resolved.
GOLD Gold prices slumped to a four-and-quarter year low
at $334.00 an ounce Friday, leading COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures down across the board, traders said.

"We've seen good Australian producer hedging this week, continued fund selling, and the execution of some stop loss orders around $336.00 in the bullion market," Credit Lyonnais Rouse's New York chief bullion dealer, Scott Mehlman, said.
"With the Hong Kong market closed next week for a holiday, there aren't going to be the usual buyers around either, so gold prices will probably go lower still," he said.

Commodity fund selling has accelerated this week as the four year low at $336.00, seen in January this year, came under pressure again, while Australian gold miners took advantage of a slide in the Australian dollar to hedge their positions by selling more gold forward, bullion dealers said.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed sharply lower and notched new lows on prospects for a resumption soon of active harvesting of the U.S. winter wheat crop, traders said. New-crop July set a new contract low of $3.25 a bushel, below the previous low of $3.28 set Monday.
The $3.25 level is also a new three-year low and is the lowest level for a nearby contract since $3.03-1/2 was hit in July 1994.

Showers this week slowed combining of the Kansas wheat crop but there are signs harvesting soon will be back to full speed amid hot and drier weather. The soft red winter harvest also is gaining speed in the southernmost reaches of the SRW Belt.

CSCE sugar futures closed an active session weaker Friday as speculators continued to roll spot July contracts into the back months ahead of first notice day, traders said. The spot month closed 0.19 cent lower at 10.92 cents, traded 11.13 to 10.91 cents.
